proposal.title: 5. SSG General Ledger — Correct Abacus 1.x scope and retain later Abacus 2 integration
proposal.reason: Replace the former BPI scenario with the author-requested independent SSG General Ledger partnership. Use the confirmed story dates: agreement 1977-07-28, team/development 1977-08-12, vanilla CP/M/CBASIC release 1978-01-15 and joint AION C/General Ledger Aurelia launch on the morning of 1978-06-06. SSG retains application ownership and sales; AION funds bounded porting and later networking work, not an equity investment. Preserve stable legacy record IDs for reference and review continuity; displayed identities and product scope are SSG General Ledger. Exact original GL/runtime revisions and speed ratios remain unverified. See review_evidence/ssg-general-ledger for source distinctions, scope and validation. Revised against author feedback change_review.1065e77b-8905-4302-a025-0d92b6b6738f: Abacus 1.x, including the Model II edition, must not claim Pulse access or formatted table/report layouts. Remove the legacy programmatic-file-access claim and printed-form feature as well as correcting chapters 1 and 2. Retain the direct SSG summary-file import into ordinary worksheet cells. Abacus 2 retains its later Pulse and report/layout capabilities; no advanced Abacus 3 storage/query features are moved into 1.x. Original before snapshots and feedback history remain unchanged.

data_interchange.contract: Import versioned BPI disk-file summaries as independent planning inputs: named columns, account identifiers, period, currency, decimal amounts and reconciliation totals. Validate parsing, rounding, memory and save/reopen. No direct ledger write-back, live database link or simultaneous execution.

chapters.description: Abacus stores one sparse worksheet per document, with formulas and editor-consistent navigation. Spreadsheet data can populate printed forms and layouts.

Pulse can edit supported closed Abacus files offline, preserving formulas and versioned features while excluding concurrent writers and invalidating stale cached results.

Versioned disk summaries from {accounting_export_id} supply independent planning inputs with named columns, account identifiers, period, currency, decimal amounts and reconciliation totals. Validate parsing, rounding, memory and save/reopen. This is not ledger write-back, live database access or simultaneous BPI execution.

The implementation uses {portable_api_id}. Keep application/document algorithms separate from platform adapters; query display dimensions and attributes, use semantic colours and clipping, and handle allocation failures with bounded buffers and banked-object handles. Persistent records are explicitly encoded and versioned rather than raw structures or pointers. Recompile and adapt OS-specific modules for another target, then test its resource limits; source portability does not extend the list of qualified hosts.

This application suite targets Z80/CP/M on {host_base_computer_aurelia} and {host_base_computer_aurelia_plus}. The recorded installed-RAM requirement is {minimum_ram_kib} KiB. It requires {runtime_cpm_aurelia}. The edition is delivered on diskette. Application workspace and ROM footprint remain unspecified.
